Where things stand

Search for Coastside today and there's not much to find.

There's no site that shows what Coastside does. Instagram shows the work, but not your crew size, the coating systems you use, the sectors you cover or how to brief you on a job. A builder or architect needs all of that before they add a new plasterer to their list.

How trade work is won

Builders don't hire a plasterer once. They find one they can keep using.

One builder or architect who trusts your finish can send you years of work. The site's job is to get Coastside onto their list and keep it there.

Why this version

Why this is the one for Coastside.

We built and tested several directions before landing here. This is the one we would put Coastside's name on, for four reasons.

01

It reads like a commercial contractor.

The copy talks the way estimators and project managers work: specification, program, sequencing, documentation and handover. A builder reading it sees a crew that can take a whole package, not a plasterer who does houses. That is what puts Coastside in the running for bigger jobs.

02

It looks like the world architects work in.

Restrained type, full-screen photography and a charcoal, bronze and stone palette. It sits comfortably next to the stone and surface suppliers architects and designers already specify from. A premium finish trade should look like one. A template site tells an architect you are priced like one.

03

The work does the selling.

The site opens full screen on finished work, and every project, service and area page leads with photography. In a trade judged on the finish, a good photo of a facade says more than any sentence we could write.

04

The full Builder system sits underneath.

Case studies, service and area pages, the builder pack, the capability statement, a quote form that takes plans and tender dates, the tender list sign-up and your enquiry dashboard. It looks premium and it works hard. Nothing here is a mockup: every page clicks through.

A builder decides in seconds whether you are a crew for their size of job. This version answers that before they scroll.

What we need from you

Six things that make the difference.

Builders trust names and places they recognise. These are what turn a good-looking site into one that wins work.

01

5 to 6 recent projects

Photos, the suburb, the builder or architect (with their OK), the system used and one thing that made the job hard. A 20-minute chat covers it.

02

2 to 3 references

A sentence or two from builders or designers you work with regularly.

03

Crew on site

Real photos of the team on real jobs. Nothing reads better to a builder.

04

Your numbers

Years in business, crew size, projects completed and sectors covered. We only publish what's accurate.

05

Licence and insurance

QBCC licence number, certificates of currency and where you work, so the builder pack is complete.

06

Where enquiries go

The email address you want quote requests sent to.
